about: The external services a project may call (M10.2): the packages it imports and the environment names it reads that reveal each, and how the isolated copy stands in for it. `stub` says what the copy gives the app in its place; null means only a real account answers, so the flows through it are said as not covered (`why`). Read by eaos/analysis/experience/domain_data.py.

services.stub: the copy sends its mail to the run's own mail catcher (Mailpit, {mail_port}): every mail is kept and read there, none leaves

services.why: mail sent through SendGrid's API, not SMTP: only a real SendGrid account delivers it, the run's mail catcher never sees it
mail sent through Resend's API, not SMTP: only a real Resend account delivers it
mail sent through Postmark's API, not SMTP: only a real Postmark account delivers it
mail sent through Mailgun's API, not SMTP: only a real Mailgun account delivers it
a payment needs the owner's Stripe test-mode keys, which a run never holds: the copy gets a key of its own that Stripe refuses
a payment needs the owner's PayPal sandbox account, which a run never holds
a payment needs the owner's Lemon Squeezy test store, which a run never holds
a text message needs the owner's Twilio account, which a run never holds
a model's answer needs the owner's OpenAI key, which a run never holds
a model's answer needs the owner's Anthropic key, which a run never holds
a model's answer needs the owner's Google AI key, which a run never holds
a map draws only with the owner's Google Maps key, which a run never holds
a map draws only with the owner's Mapbox token, which a run never holds
an upload needs the owner's storage bucket, which a run never holds
an upload needs the owner's Cloudinary account, which a run never holds

services.stub: the copy gets an address of its own for Sentry: errors are reported nowhere, and no step of a user waits on them
the copy gets a key of its own for PostHog: the events go nowhere, and no step of a user waits on them
